subj: I tried counting reps from an accelerometer
value: Build: IMU rep counter + bar speed, 9/10 sets exact count, ~7% speed error on generated data
body:
Fort tracking strength workouts automatically made me curious how hard rep counting is from motion data alone, so I built a small version: it counts reps and estimates bar speed from an accelerometer, however the sensor is rotated.

On 10 generated sets with known answers it got the rep count exactly right on 9 and bar speed within about 7%. The README is honest about where it breaks (slow reps read 10 to 15% fast, and two reps that run together count as one): github.com/Venkat960407/rep-counter-imu
proof: I'm Venkat, a high school programmer in Redmond. I write the autonomous code for my VEX robotics team (C++, PID, odometry, IMU and rotation sensors), and we're ranked 12th in the world in Robot Skills.

subj: Where one drone stops being enough
value: Build: one-drone herding sim; 20 head 100%, 40 head ~80%, 80 head 0% in 30 min
body:
Brumby's drones herding cattle got me wondering where a single drone hits its limit, so I built a small simulator using the collect-and-drive strategy from shepherding research.

One drone pens 20 head every time in about 4 minutes and 40 head about 80% of the time, but 80 head never: the herd splits and the drone zigzags between the two groups. Code and results: github.com/Venkat960407/drone-herding-sim

I'm sure your real system is far past this, but I'd love to hear where my model is wrong.
